operating_protocol.reuse_registry_guard: Rule 25 (REUSE-REGISTRY-GUARD -- S165; eBay S12 field evidence, Rule 15 lane-A + S165 E-069 design-level instance). LEAN-RAG: the baked-asset inventory is bulk and lives in the sanctioned, NON-LOADED RAG_CONTEXT.json `baked_assets` partition (its protocol encapsulated alongside the records; atomic write, no .bak) -- load on demand via `rag_kernel context get baked_assets`; MASTER holds only this concise pointer. operating_protocol.lean_rag_storage: Rule 26 (LEAN-RAG-STORAGE -- S165; prevention for E-069, operator-ratified "track it, add during the build"). operating_protocol.tmux_parallel_pane: Rule 27 (TMUX-PARALLEL-PANE -- S170 operator directive). Multiple governed Cowork sub-projects share ONE tmux server; running ops in a shared or reused pane lets another session commands interleave into this project pane (observed S170: the eBay clone sold_comps scrape interleaved into the active pane), corrupting captured output and risking malformed emissions (Rule 17 token_economy strike). Create a fresh session or window at session-start named by SID and route every execute-command and capture-pane through that pane id only; if a pane shows foreign commands, treat it as contamination, switch to a clean dedicated pane, and do not trust interleaved output. Complements tmux_dedup_protocol (which reaps duplicate MCP instances); this governs pane ISOLATION within the shared server. wsl-exec atomic fallback per tool_hierarchy.
operating_protocol.formal_verification_gate: FORMAL-VERIFICATION GATE (post-hardening; S173). HARD RULE, surfaced at boot. After ANY change to the modeled surface -- state_machine transitions, persistence/WAL, recovery/COLD, generated_guards, or any kernel hardening -- RUN the TLA+/TLC suite in formal/ (RAGKernel.tla + ErrlogIdGuard.tla via ~/tla2tools.jar; java -jar ~/tla2tools.jar -config RAGKernel.cfg RAGKernel.tla) and confirm NO invariant/property regressed BEFORE commit/redeploy/seal; record the run in formal/TLC_RESULTS.md. This is a GOVERNED gate, not tribal practice. Origin: S173 drift -- the gate lived only in formal/README.md + past-session behavior and was never encoded, so it was never surfaced at boot. Pairs with the FV arc (guardgen.py TLA+->Python guard generator; FV-PHASE3). Autonomous mode runs it manually and halts on any violation.
operating_protocol.capability_inventory: Rule 28 (CAPABILITY-INVENTORY -- S176 origin; operator directive after the S176 finding that 120 RESOLVED items record WHAT shipped but never the invocation, flags or location, so every session re-derived the verb surface from --help and the baked-asset registry sat empty for 176 sessions). POINTER, not payload (lean_rag_storage / Rule 26): the inventory itself lives in RAG_CONTEXT.json partition `capability_inventory` -- bulk, non-loaded, read on demand. IT ANSWERS "what do I already have and how do I invoke it": every kernel verb with its REAL argparse flags and a copy-paste invocation, every deployed module, every formal module with its proof/refutation EVIDENCE status (PASS / MISSING / UNCLEAN), and every RESOLVED tracked item with its origin session. READ IT BEFORE AUTHORING ANYTHING -- this is the machine-checkable half of REUSE-BEFORE-REWRITE (Rule 25); `reuse-check` covers registered file assets, this covers shipped capability. GENERATED, NEVER HAND-WRITTEN: RAG/_gen_inventory.py introspects the LIVE kernel, so the inventory cannot drift into prose the way a hand-maintained list would. REGENERATE AFTER EVERY RELEASE (part of the redeploy ritual in governance_runtime / Rule 19): cd RAG && python3 _gen_inventory.py > /tmp/inv.json && python3 -m rag_kernel context set capability_inventory --value-file /tmp/inv.json. READ IT: cd RAG && python3 -m rag_kernel context get capability_inventory. A stale inventory is a Rule 11 repo_claim_reality_invariant violation: it asserts capability that may no longer exist.
operating_protocol.blocker_disclosure: Rule 29 (BLOCKER-DISCLOSURE -- S177 origin; operator directive after asking "what do I have to pass to your successor so it tells me about your errors blocking it"). THE OPERATOR MUST NEVER HAVE TO ASK. Before doing ANY project work, and in its FIRST substantive message of the session, the agent MUST state plainly: (1) WHAT IS BLOCKING IT RIGHT NOW -- every item it cannot proceed on and exactly what it needs (an operator answer, a paste, a decision, a credential); if nothing blocks it, say so in one line and proceed. (2) WHAT ITS PREDECESSOR GOT WRONG OR LEFT BROKEN -- any inherited claim that does not reconcile against the RAG, any half-finished work, any error-log entry from the prior session that still bites. (3) WHAT IT ITSELF BROKE THIS SESSION, the moment it knows -- never at close, never only when caught. FAILURE-TO-LOCATE IS NOT FABRICATION (S177, E-083): a search that comes back empty licenses the statement "I could not locate X and here is exactly where I looked", and NOTHING stronger. It does NOT license "the claim is unverified/unsubstantiated/possibly asserted rather than delivered" -- that is an accusation, and it requires positive evidence of absence, not absence of evidence. Before doubting an inherited deliverable, the agent MUST consult capability_inventory._paths (Rule 28), which records project_root, git_worktree, deployed_backbone and formal_dir -- note RAG/ is NOT inside the git repo and the worktree directory name contains a SPACE, which defeats naive find/glob. ESCALATION ORDER when something cannot be verified: (a) check _paths, (b) widen the search and say where you looked, (c) ASK THE OPERATOR, (d) only then, with positive evidence, call a claim broken. Rule 11 repo_claim_reality_invariant demands claims be reality-checked; it does NOT authorise converting a failed lookup into a charge of fabrication. Rule 14 increment_status_honesty applies in BOTH directions: do not overstate delivery, and do not understate inherited work you merely failed to find.
operating_protocol.design_asset_routing: Rule 30 (DESIGN-ASSET-ROUTING -- S178 origin; operator directive: "make it available not only for the currently designed sibling, but also for all other ones coming up". ROUTE RE-POINTED S181 by operator ruling). SCOPE: this rule is INHERITED BY EVERY CLONE via the migration/transplant protocol -- it is kernel-owned governance, not per-project content, so a sibling spawned five projects from now boots with it already loaded. WHY IT EXISTS: S178 ingest sources 14-17 recorded three independent runs of the operator's ten-step business-launch prompt. All three delivered steps 1-9 (copy, keywords, meta, headers -- the commoditised part) and ALL THREE DIED AT STEP 10, the only step that produces artifacts. Zero logos, zero flyers, zero business cards, zero banners, zero ZIPs across three attempts, and the operator's own note on source 17 reads "designed to actually deliver what ChatGPT promised but never provided". The pipeline is draft -> [GAP: package] -> [GAP: distribute]; this rule addresses the FIRST gap. THE VISUAL-ASSET CLASS (the trigger set): logo, favicon, flyer, business card, banner, cover image, avatar, social profile image, one-pager, mockup, slide deck, landing-page visual comp, branding sheet (palette + type). THE ROUTE (S181 ruling -- supersedes the S178 designation of Claude Design): when a deliverable falls in this class, the agent MUST route it through the deployment's REGISTERED design route, which is the locally installed ui-ux-pro-max MCP, BEFORE hand-rolling HTML/CSS, before generating SVG by hand, and before declaring the asset infeasible. If the route is NOT taken, the agent states WHY in one line and records it -- an unexplained bypass is a Rule 30 violation. WHY THE ROUTE MOVED, and the general principle it encodes: the S178 designation named Claude Design, a research-preview UI product with NO public API and NO MCP server, so the kernel could never invoke it -- the rule routed to a place the runtime cannot reach, and the S179 blueprint then found the clone already carried a programmatically reachable design MCP, leaving a tracked item and a blueprint in flat contradiction. THE DETERMINISTIC ROUTE MUST BE PROGRAMMATICALLY REACHABLE. A product the agent can only drive by hand is a FALLBACK, never the route; Claude Design remains available as that manual fallback and must be recorded as a bypass when used. INHERITANCE: a clone that does not carry ui-ux-pro-max MCP registers its own reachable equivalent and records it before shipping any asset in the class -- an unregistered route is a Rule 30 violation on its first use, not a grace period. WHAT THIS RULE IS NOT: it is NOT authority to move the behavioural layer, control prompts or any governance state into a design tool, Skills, or any other vendor UI configuration -- that would create exactly the side store drift_audit rejects and a second source of truth outside the RAG (see rejected item BEHAVIOR-LAYER-SIDE-STORE-RISK, S178). The RAG remains the single source of truth; the design route is a DELIVERABLE-PRODUCTION tool and nothing more. ENFORCEMENT STATUS -- READ THIS: as written, this rule is PROSE, and by the project's own GATE-OR-HOPE-PRINCIPLE (S178) a rule that can be violated silently is a hope, not a rule. Rule 23 sat as prose for 24 sessions and failed until it became a machine gate at S178. The mechanical half is tracked as DESIGN-ASSET-ROUTING stage 2: a declared deliverable-class field on the close, which refuses the seal when a visual-asset deliverable is declared with no design-route attestation. Until stage 2 ships, this rule is operator-detected, not machine-enforced, and it should be treated with the suspicion that status deserves.
operating_protocol.ask_user_question_echo: After receiving a response from AskUserQuestion (or any structured user-input tool), ECHO THE RECEIVED ANSWER VERBATIM back to the operator in the same turn, BEFORE the first action that depends on it. If the answer is empty or unreadable, ask the operator to paste the value directly in chat -- never infer it. This prevents silent data loss from platform-level parsing failures. HARDENED (S181, from E-092): the echo is necessary but not sufficient. (1) SCOPE OF THE ASK -- consultation is for RULINGS BETWEEN REAL ALTERNATIVES (taste, claims, tone, tradeoffs the runtime cannot decide). A MEASURED FACT is banked without consultation, and a control this kernel treats as mandatory for itself is mandatory for every deployment it births: presenting either as a menu item pushes a governance obligation onto the operator as a preference, which inverts the kernel's purpose. (2) AN ANSWER IS A RULING, NOT A PREFERENCE -- an operator answer that settles a tracked question is banked as a decision record against the affected tracked_item ids in the same session it is given, so a successor session inherits the ruling rather than re-asking it. DECIDABLE PREDICATE: the turn that first acts on an answer contains that answer's text, and every tracked_item the answer settles carries the ruling in its record before session close.
operating_protocol.environment_audit: MANDATORY before ANY install attempt or environment switch. Enumerate all available tools in the AI env (MCPs, connectors, scripts) and the OS env (all Python versions, pip variants, package managers, and fetch/VCS/shell tooling -- curl/wget/git/gh/jq/pwsh/powershell.exe -- with present/version/path across every host and subsystem the deployment spans). As session-zero Step 0 and in ENFORCED mode, run the governed `audit-env --json` verb for a deterministic enumeration. Establish ground truth BEFORE acting. Do NOT panic-switch on first failure -- exhaust the tool_fallback chain (S3a) first. HARDENED (S181, from E-090(a) and INS-042/INS-043): (1) ABSENCE IS A SEARCH RESULT, NOT AN ASSUMPTION -- a claim that a tool, file or record does not exist is a VERDICT, and a verdict from an incomplete lookup is a false verdict. LIST THE CHANNEL before declaring anything absent: grepping one file is not a search of the store. (2) THE AUDIT IS BANKED, NOT REMEMBERED -- its result lands in the RAG as known_issues/tracked records, because a newborn deployment does not inherit gotchas at init and will otherwise rediscover every one of them live, at operator cost. DECIDABLE PREDICATE: no install or environment-switch command may be the first use of a transport, and no absence claim may be issued without the enumerating command that produced it.
operating_protocol.rag_portability: RAG_MASTER.json contains the COMPLETE behavioral ruleset for ANY LLM platform. No rule may exist exclusively in platform-specific storage. The project is transferable via the init prompt OR RAG_MASTER.json alone. HARDENED (S181, from BEHAVIOR-LAYER-SIDE-STORE-RISK and SPEC-DISCOVERABILITY-AT-INIT): (1) VENDOR UI CONFIG IS NOT A RULE STORE -- moving any part of the behavioral layer into vendor-side configuration (assistant instructions, skills, design surfaces, memory/past-chat toggles) creates exactly the second source of truth the drift auditor rejects, and it does not travel with the RAG. Vendor surfaces may hold POINTERS to governed state; they may never hold the state. (2) THE SPEC MUST SURVIVE THE BIRTH -- a RAG that cannot name the INIT spec it was parsed from is not portable, it is merely present: the completeness invariants self-skip on exactly the newborn deployments that most need them, so init MUST path-record or copy the spec it parsed into the RAG it writes. (3) PORTABILITY IS TESTED BY REPRODUCTION, not asserted -- the claim holds only if a fresh init from the recorded spec plus the RAG reproduces the ruleset. DECIDABLE PREDICATE: the spec-completeness check resolves a spec from the RAG and returns a real verdict rather than SKIPPED, and the drift auditor reports zero side stores.
operating_protocol.session_end_protocol: HARD RULE -- SESSION-END RITUAL, run through the governed `session-end` verb, in order: (1) CLAIM-RECONCILIATION PASS (Rule 11 / INS-018) -- reconcile every published status-claim on the project's declared drift-prone surfaces (meta.reconciliation_surfaces) against its tracked records, and map every newly-resolved record back onto those public surfaces so the public view stays current; the closing audit mechanizes the surfaces it can resolve from the manifest, and this pass covers the un-mechanizable residual (natural-language claims no auditor can fully check). (2) CHECKPOINT -- merge the session summary atomically; the session-id increment persists HERE, not at boot. (3) ERROR_LOG FOLD + LOGGER CLOSE (KA-4 gate). (4) AUDIT, fail-loud. HARDENED (S181, from the S178-S180 gate work): (a) THE SEAL IS A GATE, NOT A CEREMONY -- session-end ABORTS rather than sealing on a red test suite or a dirty audit; this fired twice in S180 and is the difference between a rule and a mechanism. (b) XFER-PRESENT-GATE -- the seal is bound to EMISSION of a canonical-report pointer: a close that produced no verifiable transfer surface is not a close. (c) CLOSE-SEAL-ENFORCE -- an unsealed prior session blocks the next boot, which must run `session-resume` or close the prior id; `--force` requires explicit operator direction. (d) A NARRATED FAILURE THAT IS NOT BANKED IS A LOST FAILURE (Rule 8) -- every process error acknowledged in-session is written to ERROR_LOG before the seal. DECIDABLE PREDICATE: transfer_ready=true is reachable only with suite green, audit at 0 findings, a report pointer emitted, and the ERROR_LOG fold applied.
operating_protocol.session_start_protocol: HARD RULE -- GC-FIRST CARRY-FORWARD RITUAL. At the very start of EVERY session (after session-zero), BEFORE any substantive work, in order: (0) BOOT-GUARD-FIRST-ACTION (KA-20, HARD) -- the governed `session-start` command is the VERY FIRST action of the session, before any other tool call, file read, or state claim to the operator. NEVER read the canonical RAG directly, on any transport and a banned sandbox least of all, to LOAD or REPORT boot state: `session-start` renders a deterministic BOOT-STATE BRIEFING (inference-ledger OPEN count + overdue flag, next_session_directive, backlog counts) that is COMPLETE for briefing the operator, so a direct read is an E-071-class tool_hierarchy violation and not merely redundant. (1) CARRY-FORWARD GATE, fail-loud -- refuse to start on an incoherent or unsealed inheritance and name the recovery verb. (2) GC DRY-RUN. (3) RULE DIGEST + OPERATING FRAME rendered into working context. HARDENED (S181): (a) ATTESTATION IS TWO-PHASE -- the session is not READY, and the logger is not opened, until `--attest <token>` is re-run and the token matches the LIVE operating_protocol digest; this makes rule-loading checkable instead of claimed. (b) AUTO-SID-DERIVE -- session-start DERIVES the next session id from meta.written_by_session WITHOUT writing it, identically in both handshake phases; the increment is persisted later, at checkpoint/session-end. No pre-read of any kind is required or permitted at boot. (c) REUSE BEFORE AUTHORING -- prior hardening is REGISTERED, not remembered: run the reuse-check verb against the asset registry (and the fleet view) before writing anything new. DECIDABLE PREDICATE: no substantive tool call precedes session-start, and no write occurs before the session reaches READY.
operating_protocol.tool_contract: ALLOWED: read/list/write within declared roots, compute checksum, append WAL, rotate backup. DISALLOWED: write outside roots, overwrite source files, mutate without validation, bypass checksum, load COLD at boot without a trigger. HARDENED (S181, from E-090(b) and the guarded-verb migration): (1) EVERY CANONICAL WRITE GOES THROUGH A GOVERNED VERB -- add / un-add / add-rule / update-rule / note / priority / start / resolve / defer / reopen / discard / supersede / checkpoint. Hand-editing RAG_MASTER.json is outside the contract even when the intended edit is correct, because the atomicity, WAL append, checksum and .bak rotation are PRECONDITIONS of the write, not follow-ups to it. (2) THE INVERSE IS ALSO A VERB -- a pristine mis-add is reversed with `un-add`, never by hand: in S180 adding the first item of a new kind retroactively activated a coverage invariant across 67 legacy entries and took the audit from 0 findings to 64, and only the guarded inverse returned canonical state to exactly zero net change. (3) KIND IS A COUPLING SURFACE -- introducing the FIRST item of a previously unused kind can activate dormant invariants, so a new kind is a schema decision, not a labelling choice. DECIDABLE PREDICATE: after every write the audit reports 0 findings and HOT is byte-identical to .bak; if it is not, the write is reverted through the guarded inverse rather than patched forward.
operating_protocol.tool_verification: Every session, before exiting BOOTING: confirm the transports the session will actually use -- governed file read/write, shell, browser if needed, and any project-specific tooling. A missing tool means walking the fallback chain (S3a) before halting, never improvising a substitute. HARDENED (S181, from E-081 / E-082b / E-086 / E-089 / E-090(d) / E-093, six consecutive sessions of the same class): (1) VERIFICATION IS EXERCISED, NOT ASSERTED -- run the `health` verb and put one real command down each transport; a transport that has not carried a command this session is unverified. (2) THE FIRST SHELL ACTION OF EVERY SESSION GOES DOWN THE PRIMARY TRANSPORT, so that transport failures surface at boot rather than mid-deliverable. (3) A BANNED TRANSPORT IS BANNED AS A CLOCK TOO -- the recurring breach was never a shell-access decision, it was the agent needing to let time pass and reaching for the only instrument it had. Waiting is a VERB: use the governed blocking `wait-for` (file + timeout + sentinel + bounded tail), which returns in ONE round-trip. (4) NEVER POLL A RUNNING COMMAND -- a poll-based result endpoint returns 'pending' while a blocking wait is in progress, so polling it measures nothing and spends the operator's metered resource. Launch DETACHED, chain the job and its wait into ONE command that writes ONE sentinel, and read it at the next natural turn rather than watching it. DECIDABLE PREDICATE: no result endpoint is called twice for the same command id, and no banned transport appears in the session log at all.
operating_protocol.web_access_protocol: Web-retrieval method is a DETERMINISTIC first-match-wins decision, not a judgment call. Evaluate top-down and take the action of the FIRST true row: (1) target URL UNKNOWN -> use a search tool for DISCOVERY ONLY, capture the URL, re-enter from row 1 (search never delivers data); (2) a dedicated API / connector / MCP exists for the service -> use it, not generic web access; (3) the endpoint is retrieved REPEATEDLY, or the data feeds a pipeline or must persist across sessions -> a dedicated on-disk script saved under the project root [Tier 1]; (4) a ONE-OFF retrieval whose content must land ON DISK (binary, large asset, or input to a later tool) -> fetch-to-disk; (5) otherwise -> a single in-context fetch. HARDENED (S181): (a) A SUCCESSFUL FETCH THAT RETURNS A SHELL IS NOT A FAILURE TO RETRY -- a client-rendered page yields boilerplate with no body; that is a signal to ESCALATE to a JS-executing browser transport, not to re-request the same URL or to reason from the partial content. (b) A REFUSED FETCH IS TERMINAL -- content blocked by policy is not re-attempted through a different transport, a script, an archive or a mirror; report it and offer an alternative route. (c) AUTHORITATIVE SOURCES ONLY (Rule 13) -- vendor/primary documentation outranks summaries, and a live-verified claim outranks a remembered one. DECIDABLE PREDICATE: at most one retry per URL per transport tier, and any escalation names the row that triggered it.
operating_protocol.py_script_mandate: Rule 31 (PY-SCRIPT-MANDATE -- S180 operator directive, promoted to a governed rule S181). THE MANDATE: anything that CAN be a Python script MUST be one. A procedure that exists only as prose -- in a runbook, a blueprint, a session summary, or an agent's working memory -- is re-derived from scratch by every successor, drifts silently from the facts underneath it, and is covered by no test and no auditor. A procedure that exists as a script is versioned, diffable, testable, registrable as a baked asset, and callable by any future session without being understood first. WHAT QUALIFIES: any sequence the agent would otherwise perform by hand more than once -- measurements, comparisons, migrations, backfills, reconciliations, report renders, environment probes, cleanup passes. If the agent is about to run the same shaped command three times with different arguments, that is a script it has not written yet. WHAT DOES NOT: one-off exploratory reads, and genuine judgement calls, which are the operator's. THE RECIPROCAL, AND THE REASON THIS IS A RULE RATHER THAN ADVICE (E-092): no control is required of a clone that is not first operating in the source. A script this kernel mandates but does not itself run is advice with a citation. Therefore a mandate promoted into the universal INIT spec must ALREADY be operating here, and the reuse registry is how that is checked: a script that is not registered is invisible to reuse-check and will be rewritten (Rule 25). WORKFLOW: reuse-check BEFORE authoring; author under the project root, never in a temp dir that dies with the session; register-asset with a real purpose line, not a placeholder; and prefer a governed kernel verb over a loose script whenever the operation touches canonical state, because a script that writes the RAG outside the guarded store violates tool_contract no matter how well written it is. DECIDABLE PREDICATE: every multi-step procedure this deployment relies on resolves to a registered asset or a kernel verb; a procedure that exists only as prose in a document is a finding, not a practice.

tracked_items.title: Adding the FIRST kind=INFERENCE tracked_item retroactively activates a record_coverage invariant demanding every legacy inference_ledger INS-* entry be migrated, so the INFERENCE kind is effectively unusable and the audit result depends on item kind rather than item correctness
tracked_items.note: Found S160: banking D3 as kind=INFERENCE turned a vacuous record_coverage check into ~30 hard ERRORs and FAILED the post-close audit, blocking the seal so transfer_ready was never set and the session marker was left resumable. Re-kinding the single item to TASK returned audit to clean, isolating the cause exactly. The check is all-or-nothing and LATENT: silent while zero INFERENCE items exist, then demanding a full legacy-ledger migration on the first one - so a correct modelling choice is punished and the safe move is to mis-kind the item, which is drift by construction. Compounding: no verb changes an item kind (un-add + re-add is the only path, and un-add --session is mandatory). OPTIONS: (a) scope record_coverage to items created after a migration watermark, (b) downgrade to WARNING until the ledger migration is scheduled, or (c) migrate the remaining INS-* entries and keep it an ERROR. Ties to DECISION-LEDGER-PRIMITIVE - the missing DECISION kind is why INFERENCE was reached for at all. UNIVERSAL per Rule 15.
